title: How much does a seed move a number?
promptMarkdown:
A classifier is evaluated on a held-out test set of $n=200$ items and gets 180 right, an observed accuracy of $\hat p=0.90$. Treat the test items as independent draws and the model's true accuracy $p$ as fixed.

1. Model the number of correct predictions as a binomial random variable. Derive the standard error of $\hat p$ and evaluate it at $p=0.9$, $n=200$ (three significant figures). Give an approximate 95% interval for $p$.
2. A second model, trained from a different random seed, gets 183 right ($0.915$). Compare the 1.5-point gap with the single-model uncertainty as a rough diagnostic. Explain why this is not a complete test of their difference, which paired outcomes are missing, and what statistic you would compute from them. Do not assume a sign for the covariance of their correctness outcomes.
3. How large must a test set be for the standard error of an accuracy near $0.9$ to be at most $0.005$? Show the inequality you solve.
4. In two or three sentences: why does the same architecture trained from five different seeds give five different test accuracies on a fixed test set, and what must a report contain so that a reader can tell signal from seed noise?

**The information contract for this evaluation.**

1. **Observed:** one trained classifier's predictions for 200 held-out test items, with their labels.
2. **Prediction target:** the label of each test item.
3. **History in training:** the classifier was trained without any of the 200 test items.
4. **History at inference:** each test item's own features.
5. **Person:** not applicable; every test item is unseen in training.
6. **Task:** familiar; the test items are drawn from the same distribution as the training items.
7. **Later time periods:** not tested; the items are treated as independent draws, so nothing here concerns later data.
8. **Unavailable in real use:** none, provided the test set is used once; choosing among models by it would leak, as in exercise 1.
9. **Simplest baseline:** the majority class; part 2 compares two trained models instead.
10. **Claims not tested:** accuracy under another distribution, on later data, or for any model other than the one evaluated.
hintLadder: A difference of accuracies between two models evaluated on the same items is not the difference of two independent estimates. Which items carry information about the difference: those both models get right, or those where they disagree?
List what changes between two runs that differ only in the seed: initial weights, mini-batch order, dropout masks, augmentation draws. Each changes the function learned.

deterministicChecks.description: the standard error 0.0212 (about 2.1 percentage points) appears

criteria.criterion: Standard error derived from the binomial variance as sqrt(p(1−p)/n) and evaluated as 0.0212.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Value correct without derivation, or derivation with an arithmetic slip.

criteria.criterion: An approximate 95% interval of about 0.90 ± 0.04 (normal approximation), stated with its approximation named.

Treats the marginal gap as a rough diagnostic only; asks for same-item discordant counts or paired differences, and avoids assuming that same-item accuracies always have positive covariance or a universally smaller paired standard error.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Both the noise conclusion and the pairing argument are correct.

levels.label: not met
levels.description: Claims the second model is better, or no pairing argument.

criteria.criterion: Names the seed-dependent sources of variation and requires reports to give the number of seeds, mean and spread, and the test-set standard error, never a best-of-k seed.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Sources and reporting requirements both correct.

checkExamples.label: wrong variance
checkExamples.text: The standard error is 0.0045 and the test set must have at least 360 items.

checkExamples.label: percentage form
checkExamples.text: The standard error is about 2.1 percentage points, so a one-point gap is noise. A test set of 3,600 items brings it down to half a point.
